## Contents

# [[edit](/wiki/RIBA_plan_of_work "Edit section: What is the RIBA plan of work?")] What is the **RIBA plan of work**?

The [RIBA Plan of Work](https://www.architecture.com/knowledge-and-resources/resources-landing-page/riba-plan-of-work) is published by the [Royal Institute of British Architects](/wiki/Royal_Institute_of_British_Architects "Royal Institute of British Architects") ([RIBA](/wiki/RIBA "RIBA")). The latest version is also is endorsed by the [Chartered Institute of Architectural Technologists](/wiki/Chartered_Institute_of_Architectural_Technologists "Chartered Institute of Architectural Technologists"), the [Construction Industry Council](/wiki/Construction_Industry_Council "Construction Industry Council"), the Royal Incorporation of [Architects](/wiki/Architects "Architects") in [Scotland](/wiki/Scotland "Scotland"), the Royal [Society](/wiki/Society "Society") of [Architects](/wiki/Architects "Architects") in [Wales](/wiki/Wales "Wales") and the Royal [Society](/wiki/Society "Society") of Ulster [Architects](/wiki/Architects "Architects").

It was originally launched in 1963 as a [fold](/wiki/Fold "Fold") out [sheet](/wiki/Sheet "Sheet") that illustrated the roles of [participants](/wiki/Participants "Participants") in [design](/wiki/Design "Design") and [construction](/wiki/Construction "Construction") in a simple [matrix](/wiki/Matrices "Matrices") format. The first detailed [plan of work](/wiki/Plan_of_work "Plan of work") was published in 1964 (ref. Introduction, **RIBA Plan of Work** 2007).

# [[edit](/wiki/RIBA_plan_of_work "Edit section: How is the RIBA plan of work structured?")] How is the **RIBA plan of work** structured?

Split into a number of key [project stages](/wiki/Project_stages "Project stages"), the **RIBA Plan of Work** provides a shared [framework](/wiki/Framework "Framework") for [design](/wiki/Design "Design") and [construction](/wiki/Construction "Construction") that [offers](/wiki/Offer "Offer") both a [process](/wiki/Process "Process") [map](/wiki/Map "Map") and a [management](/wiki/Management "Management") [tool](/wiki/Tools "Tools"). Whilst it has never been clear that [architects](/wiki/Architects "Architects") actually follow the [detail](/wiki/Details "Details") of the [plan](/wiki/Plan "Plan") in their day to day [activities](/wiki/Activities "Activities"), the [work stages](/wiki/Work_stages "Work stages") have been used as a means of designating stage [payments](/wiki/Payment "Payment") and identifying [team](/wiki/Team "Team") [members](/wiki/Member "Member") responsibilities when assessing [insurance](/wiki/Insurance "Insurance") [liabilities](/wiki/Liability "Liability"), and they commonly appear in contracts and [appointment documents](/wiki/Appointment_document "Appointment document").

The [Plan of Work](/wiki/Plan_of_work "Plan of work") has evolved through its history to reflect the increasing [complexity](/wiki/Complexity "Complexity") of [projects](/wiki/Project "Project"), to incorporate increasing and changing [regulatory](/wiki/Regulatory "Regulatory") requirements and to reflect the demands of industry and [government](/wiki/Government "Government") [reports](/wiki/Report "Report") criticising the industry. It has moved from a simple [matrix](/wiki/Matrices "Matrices") representing just the [traditional procurement route](/wiki/Traditional_procurement_route "Traditional procurement route"), to include multiple [procurement routes](/wiki/Procurement_routes "Procurement routes"), more diverse roles, [multi-disciplinary teams](/wiki/Multi-disciplinary_team "Multi-disciplinary team"), [government](/wiki/Government "Government") [gateways](/wiki/Gateways "Gateways") and stages that take [place](/wiki/Place "Place") before and after [design](/wiki/Design "Design") and [construction](/wiki/Construction "Construction"). It is supported by other [RIBA](/wiki/RIBA "RIBA") publications such as the [RIBA](/wiki/RIBA "RIBA") Job Book, and supplements, such as a [sustainability](/wiki/Sustainability "Sustainability") overlay and a [green](/wiki/Green "Green") overlay.

# [[edit](/wiki/RIBA_plan_of_work "Edit section: What work stages does the latest RIBA plan of work include?")] What [work stages](/wiki/Work_stages "Work stages") does the latest **RIBA plan of work** include?

The latest version of the **RIBA plan of work**, published in 2020, reflects increasing requirements for [sustainability](/wiki/Sustainability "Sustainability") and [Building Information Modelling](/wiki/Building_Information_Modelling "Building Information Modelling") ([BIM](/wiki/Bim "Bim")).

In addition, the [work stages](/wiki/Work_stages "Work stages") were re-structured and re-named.:

# [[edit](/wiki/RIBA_plan_of_work "Edit section: Overlays to the RIBA plan of work.")] [Overlays to the RIBA plan of work](/wiki/Overlays_to_the_RIBA_plan_of_work "Overlays to the RIBA plan of work").

A number of overlays have been published to provide detailed [guidance](/wiki/Guidance "Guidance") on specific [design](/wiki/Design "Design") and [built environment](/wiki/Built_environment "Built environment") [considerations](/wiki/Consideration "Consideration") that can be implemented through each **RIBA Plan of Work** stage to enable informed [decision making](/wiki/Decision_making "Decision making") at the right time and with the right [stakeholders](/wiki/Stakeholders "Stakeholders"), to support the best [project](/wiki/Project "Project") [outcomes](/wiki/Outcome "Outcome"):

The [green](/wiki/Green "Green") overlay with reference to [Soft Landings](/wiki/Soft_landings "Soft landings") was also published in 2011 for further [information](/wiki/Information "Information") see [Green Overlay](https://www.bsria.com/uk/news/article/riba-plan-of-work-green-overlay-supports-soft-landings/)

# [[edit](/wiki/RIBA_plan_of_work "Edit section: Criticism of the RIBA plan of work")] Criticism of the **RIBA plan of work**

The **RIBA plan of work** has been criticised for continually changing the names and definitions of [project stages](/wiki/Project_stages "Project stages"), and for a lack of [co-ordination](/wiki/Co-ordination "Co-ordination") with other industry [project plans](/wiki/Project_plans "Project plans"). This can leave [clients](/wiki/Clients "Clients") and other [stakeholders](/wiki/Stakeholders "Stakeholders") confused about what terminology is being used, and what it refers to - for example, the re-naming of [detail design](/wiki/Detail_design "Detail design") as [spatial](/wiki/Spatial "Spatial") [co-ordination](/wiki/Co-ordination "Co-ordination") is not something that is widely understood.

In addition the [plan](/wiki/Plan "Plan") has been criticised for focussing too much on [the role of the architect](/wiki/The_role_of_the_architect "The role of the architect"), and not giving enough [detail](/wiki/Details "Details") about the crucial [planning](/wiki/Planning "Planning") stages that happen before an [architect](/wiki/Architects "Architects") is [appointed](/wiki/Appointed "Appointed"). Those early stages are instrumental in defining the way the [project](/wiki/Project "Project") is set up, and the nature of the [project](/wiki/Project "Project") that the [client](/wiki/Clients "Clients") intends to develop.

You can find out more about the **RIBA plan of work** at: <https://www.architecture.com/knowledge-and-resources/resources-landing-page/riba-plan-of-work>
